name: Ahrefs
summary: Terms say "we may use User Content, including any content you provide to us in connection with your use of AI Tools, to train our machine learning models"; no opt-out found.

name: Amazon Q Developer
summary: Policy text is shared across multiple company products — not verified as specific to this tool.

name: Base44
summary: Terms licence Customer Data and Generated Output "for the purpose of maintaining, providing and improving the Platform", including to "(5) train Company software tools (e.g. artificial intelligence and machine learning models)"; no training opt-out.

name: Bolt.new
summary: Bolt.new links to StackBlitz's policy, which covers "the Bolt application ( www.Bolt.new )": "Unless you opt out and subject to the regional and consent rules below, we may use Bolt Model Development Content ... to train, fine-tune, evaluate, benchmark, and improve artificial-intelligence models developed by or for StackBlitz." EEA, UK and Swiss accounts: "We do not use Bolt Model Development Content ... for AI model development".
data_retention: Personal information and user content retained while account active. Upon voluntary closure, data deleted or anonymized within 30 days (subject to backups, legal obligations, security requirements). Residual copies may persist in backups/logs for limited period.

name: Buffer
summary: Asked "Does Buffer scrape my content to train the AI?", Buffer says text entered in AI Assistant "will be shared with OpenAI" but never states whether training happens; legal pages are silent.

name: ChatGPT
summary: "When you use our services for individuals (Free, Plus, Pro), we may use your content to train our models." "To opt out, turn off Improve the model for everyone under Settings > Data controls in ChatGPT, or select Do not train on my content in our Privacy Portal." "By default, we don't use inputs or outputs from ChatGPT Business, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Edu, or our API to improve our models." Conversations you give feedback on may still be used.
data_retention: Personal Data retained as long as needed to provide Services or for legitimate business purposes including resolving disputes, safety, security, and legal compliance. Specific retention periods vary by data type: user-deletable data removed within 30 days of deletion request unless retention needed for safety/legal reasons; Temporary Chats auto-deleted within 30 days unless safety/legal reasons require retention; some data retained longer for security, safety, or legal reasons.

name: Claude
summary: Consumer plans (Free, Pro, Max): We may use your Inputs and Outputs to train and improve Anthropic AI models, unless you opt out through your account settings. Commercial plans don't train by default.
data_retention: Feedback data stored for up to 5 years in secured back-end

name: DeepL
summary: Rated on DeepL's free tier: free-tier submissions are used to train and improve DeepL's models, with no opt-out found. For DeepL Pro, API Pro and Write Pro, DeepL says "your texts will not be used to improve the quality of our services."
data_retention: Free version: texts processed for limited period to train neural networks; Pro version: texts kept temporarily only as necessary for service delivery, then deleted after contractual performance; Voice: audio data deleted after service completion

name: DeepSeek
summary: Uses Inputs and Outputs to improve its services; "you can opt out by turning off "Improve the model for everyone"."

name: ElevenLabs
summary: "We use your personal information to research, build, train and improve our AI models." "You can opt out ... by navigating to the 'Data use' menu in the 'Terms and Privacy' section of your ElevenLabs account."

name: Fireflies.ai
summary: We do not use personal information for AI model training and we contractually prohibit our vendors from using this information for their own model training.

name: Frase
summary: "Frase does not use Customer Data to develop or train generalized artificial intelligence or machine learning models".

name: Gemini
summary: Policy text is shared across multiple company products — not verified as specific to this tool.
data_retention: Default 18 months, configurable to 3 months, 36 months, or indefinite. Chats reviewed by human reviewers retained for up to three years. Some data retained until Google Account deletion.

name: GitHub Copilot
summary: Rated on Copilot Free, Pro and Pro+: "from April 24 onward we will begin using interaction data—specifically inputs, outputs, code snippets, and associated context—from Copilot Free, Pro, and Pro+ users to train and improve our AI models unless you opt out." Opt out in settings under "Privacy". GitHub says "Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise users are not affected by this update."

name: Grammarly
summary: "Product improvements include (1) training and validating our AI and machine learning models". "Product Improvement and Training is on for individual users by default." Grammarly's help page explains "How do I turn Product Improvement and Training on or off?"
data_retention: Personal data retained as long as necessary to provide products, complete transactions, comply with legal obligations, and resolve disputes. User content for troubleshooting and product improvement typically retained no longer than one year, then deleted or de-identified unless user retains it or legal obligations require longer retention.

name: Granola
summary: We only use de-identified data to train AI models, which you can opt-out of within your Granola account settings.

name: hancocyber.com
summary: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely.
data_retention: Comments and metadata retained indefinitely; comment opt-in cookies last one year; login cookies last two days; screen options cookies last one year; 'Remember Me' login persists two weeks; post edit cookie expires after 1 day

name: HeyGen
summary: HeyGen says it "may use the input that you provide us to improve our services, for example, to train and enhance the models". "You may request to opt-out of this training and enhancement by contacting us". The opt-out is by email, not an account setting.

name: HubSpot
summary: HubSpot "may use customer data ... to train and improve HubSpot's own AI models." "By default, the setting will be turned on." "Super Admins can opt out of AI model training at any time". Same terms on the free CRM.

name: Ideogram
summary: User information is used "as a matter of our legitimate interests, including ... training the models that power our Services"; the policy lists opt-outs only for marketing and analytics, not training.
data_retention: We retain your information for as long as is reasonably necessary for the purposes specified in this Privacy Policy. When determining the length of time to retain information, we consider various criteria, including whether we need the information to continue to administer your account, provide the Services, resolve a dispute, enforce our contractual agreements, prevent harm

name: InVideo
summary: "We may use your User Data to train, fine-tune or otherwise adjust the parameters of our artificial intelligence and machine-learning models. You can stop this use by deleting the relevant User Data or closing your account". There's no setting to opt out.

name: JetBrains AI Assistant
summary: "Detailed code-related data can be used for product improvement and training AI models." For the free Non-commercial licence: "We may collect analytics as specified above by default based on our legitimate interest. You may opt out in the product settings."

name: Kagi
summary: When using third party AI model providers, we are using privacy-respecting services that do not save the data or use it for training, whenever possible.
data_retention: Load Balancer Logs: 7 days; Virtual Machine Logs: 7 days; Sentry: 90 days; Assistant threads: 1 day (default, auto-delete); Reported threads: 30 days; Web page summaries: max 1 day

name: Kimi
summary: "the platform may use users' input data, instructions, and generated responses for model training". Opt-out by request: "If you do not want your conversation data to be used for training, you can contact customer support ... and submit a request."

name: Kling AI
summary: "Kling AI may process usage data, aggregated data, or Input for its lawful business purposes" including to "(f) create, test, improve, train, or otherwise develop the artificial intelligence or machine learning models ... used by Kling AI"; no training opt-out in the terms or the privacy policy.

name: Lovable
summary: Trains on Customer Content; "You can opt out of model training at any time in your account settings, on any plan, at no cost". Business/Enterprise content is not trained on.

name: Luma AI (Dream Machine)
summary: Train, develop, and improve the artificial intelligence, machine learning, and models that we use to support our Services

name: Meshy
summary: Terms (Sep 19, 2026): "Meshy may use Customer Inputs and Customer Outputs ... from non-Enterprise Customers to train, validate, test, or improve Services unless otherwise agreed to in the Order." No opt-out for Free/Pro.

name: Microsoft Copilot
summary: Policy text is shared across multiple company products — not verified as specific to this tool.

name: Mistral Vibe (formerly Le Chat)
summary: "your input and output data (such as conversations, documents, and other user-provided content) may be included in Mistral's model training programs." "Vibe: users are not opted out by default and can opt out at any time in their settings."

name: Moises
summary: "MOISES DOES NOT HAVE THE RIGHT TO AND WILL NOT USE YOUR USER CONTENT OR OUTPUT TO TRAIN OR FINE-TUNE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE OR MACHINE LEARNING MODELS UNLESS YOU HAVE EXPRESSLY AUTHORIZED SUCH USE IN WRITING OR VIA AN ELECTRONIC OPT-IN MECHANISM."

name: n8n
summary: "We do not use any personal data, including data received through any third-party services, for developing, improving, or training AI and/or ML models."

name: Notion AI
summary: By default, neither Notion nor our AI providers use your Customer Data to train any models.

name: Otter.ai
summary: Privacy policy: "training our proprietary AI technology on de-identified audio recordings and on transcriptions (which may contain Personal Information)". Otter's help centre gives an opt-out: Account Settings > Meetings > Feedback and Training, set Help improve Otter to "Don't allow sharing", and "Otter will not access your conversation for training and product improvement." The policy doesn't say whether this also covers de-identified training.

name: Perplexity AI
summary: For Free, Perplexity Pro and Perplexity Max users, AI Data Retention is enabled by default. However, these users can control whether their data is used for AI model training.

name: Photoroom
summary: "By using the Services, you acknowledge and expressly authorize Photoroom to use User Content to improve, train and develop Photoroom's products and services." "You can opt-out of this at any time by changing the settings on your account in the app under Data Control."

name: Pictory AI
summary: "Pictory will not use your Customer Content or Pictoried Content to train or fine-tune its general artificial intelligence or machine learning models, except as expressly agreed by you in writing."

name: Pika
summary: "Pika may use anonymized or aggregated Content, including Inputs, Outputs, and your interactions with the Service, and Usage Data to train, improve, and develop its machine learning models"; no training opt-out found.

name: Poe
summary: "Developers that create bots and apps on Poe using APIs may view and store your chats on their servers to train their models." Poe account settings cover model providers, not developers; no opt-out for developer training.

name: Remove.bg
summary: "We may also analyze your activity, content, media uploads and related data in your account ... to train our algorithms, models and AI products and services using machine learning to develop, improve and provide our Service." The only opt-outs offered are analytics and marketing.

name: Semrush
summary: "Semrush does not train or develop its models, and does not allow its third-party providers to train or develop its models on User Input."

name: Sourcegraph Cody
summary: Sourcegraph and Sourcegraph Partner LLMs do not use code from Cody Enterprise or Cody Pro teams to train models.
data_retention: Zero Retention: Sourcegraph Partner LLMs will not retain any input or output from the model, including embeddings, beyond the time it takes to generate the output

name: Suno
summary: Uses Submissions and other Content "to train and enhance the models that power our Services". No training opt-out is stated.

name: Tabnine
summary: "Tabnine has a *no-train-no-retain* policy." and "Tabnine does not train on your code."
data_retention: Context window deleted immediately after server returns answer. Operational metrics and logs retained for one week.

name: tl;dv
summary: "Tldx Solutions GmbH does not use Customer Content, including meeting recordings, transcripts, notes, files, or other data processed through the Services, to train, fine-tune, or improve foundation models, large language models, or other generative AI models".

name: v0
summary: Company-wide policy, not product-verified — the only available source is Vercel's general Privacy Notice, which was never scoped to v0 specifically and has no v0-specific policy text to verify facts against.

name: Writesonic
summary: "Writesonic does not use Customer Data to train or fine-tune any general-purpose, foundation, or large-language model", which "applies equally to… any Trial or free tier".

name: You.com
summary: We do not use the substance of your prompts, files, or generated outputs to train or fine-tune our own models, and our contracts with our large language model providers prohibit them from using it to train their models, except where you have separately opted in.
data_retention: User Content retained for periods described in 'Data Retention' section (specific periods not stated in provided text)

name: Zapier
summary: "Enterprise customers are automatically opted out of Zapier using their content for model training and improvement purposes. All other customers may opt out at any time."

name: Zoom AI Companion
summary: "Zoom does not use any of your audio, video, chat, screen sharing, attachments or other communications-like Customer Content (such as poll results, whiteboard and reactions) to train Zoom or third-party artificial intelligence models."
